item.itunes:summary:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZK6A7yGtmsY

值得閱讀的理由

  • 深入剖析馬斯克閃電裁撤 xAI Grok 圖像與影片團隊的背後真實原因。
  • 揭露 AI 產業在龐大算力消耗與高昂營運成本下的商業化現實困境。
  • 了解深偽技術帶來的法律風險，以及算力短缺如何衝擊高階付費用戶體驗。

摘要

突如其來的裁員風暴：Grok 圖像與影片團隊幾近瓦解

作者指出，馬斯克突如其來對旗下 xAI 的 Grok 圖像與影片團隊進行大規模裁員，約 60 至 70 名員工遭到解僱，僅留下極少數人維持基本營運，相關招聘職缺也已全面撤除。不久前馬斯克才高調利用該技術製作影片諷刺導演諾蘭，如今卻毫無預警地中止團隊推進，引發業界廣泛猜測與討論。

排除集體作弊與法律糾紛的決定性影響

作者分析，這場裁員並非源於類似 Meta 的評測榜單造假醜聞；儘管 Grok 的影像模型排名有所下滑，但並無集體舞弊跡象。在法律層面上，Grok 雖然因生成深偽影像（Deepfake）而面臨荷蘭法院高達千萬歐元的罰款禁令及美國加州的訴訟，且每月仍產出數十億張圖片與影片，但單純的官司並不足以促使馬斯克在剛發布短片後便徹底裁撤整個團隊。

算力入不敷出：付費用戶體驗惡化與成本失控

作者進一步揭露，真正迫使馬斯克痛下殺手的原因在於算力短缺與高昂營運成本。11 月初，大量每月支付 300 美元的 Super Grok Heavy 高階付費用戶紛紛抗議額度驟減、效能降級與任務出錯，退訂潮隨之爆發。馬斯克亦在社群平台上坦承，提供 Grok 服務的成本相對於收入而言高到無法持續，算力負擔已經達到極限。

資源重組的權衡：集中火力於核心產品

作者總結，雖然馬斯克積極擴建資料中心並掌握大量 GPU，但面對持續攀升的算力租賃與採購支出，極度耗費運算資源的 AI 影片與圖片生成項目顯得性價比極低。為了保證核心 Grok 模型的競爭力並履行外部算力合約，馬斯克不得不做出商業取捨，果斷割捨昂貴且無法迅速變現的圖像研發團隊。

================================================

# :00 马斯克突然裁掉Imagine团队

Musk suddenly gutted the Grok image and video team, leaving barely two people behind. Related job postings have been pulled from recruitment sites, and just recently, he was using that tech to create Odysseys to troll Nolan. Why call it quits so suddenly and shut everything down? What actually happened? Hello everyone, and welcome to Old Fen’s Storytelling YouTube channel. On November 13, the US tech media outlet The Information reported that SpaceX’s xAI laid off about 60 people from the Grok/Grok-Image team over the past week .

# :20 xAI裁员报道与岗位撤下

Only a few people were left to keep the lights on and maintain the product. Domestic news I received is even more severe, claiming the entire Grok team— about 70 people—was laid off. The slight discrepancy in these figures isn’t that important; one thing is clear: the large group previously responsible for pushing the product forward has been completely wiped out. Looking at the recruitment side, on October 6 (US time), xAI still had two openings posted: one for Grok understanding, and one for a senior.

# :20 老范判断：马斯克为什么要做算力取舍

model engineer for Grok-Image. By November 10 (Beijing time), both were taken down. How do we explain that? Could this group be involved in a collective scandal? What do I mean by a collective scandal? It means a group acting together—did they manipulate the leaderboards? Or did they lose a lawsuit , pay a penalty, and now their team is being used as a scapegoat to take the fall? My assessment is this: Musk must have made a trade-off, and the reason for that trade-off is that his computing power isn't enough to go around. He does have a lot of GPUs, but right now, using.

# :49 Imagine排名与诉讼风险

those cards to generate videos and images isn't cost-effective. He needs to rent them out to Google or OpenAI, and he needs to bet those cards on his only new product that’s actually working—which is Grok. Once you lay out the math, the teams he could previously afford to slowly cultivate are suddenly unaffordable. Let's look at how the product from this Grok team actually performed. Why, when a bunch of people were shouting, "Grok, I want to cancel my subscription," did.

# :02 生成数据与产品变化

Musk just kill off Grok? Prioritize the big project or the small one? Musk decided to prioritize the small one, as Grok is a relatively newer team. Let’s look at ByteDance and Kuaishou— those guys are thriving with micro-dramas. Musk has the X platform; why doesn't he want to turn AI into a business on X? I initially wondered about this myself: could this team have been almost entirely wiped out because of a collective scandal?

# :15 Grok Bot用户抱怨与成本

Like Meta’s Llama 3, which was a typical case of a scandal—the whole team deceived the company together to inflate their scores. It ended up embarrassing the company, and in the end, it was basically cleaned out from top to bottom. Meta's current AI team was recruited later. Grok's imaging tool shouldn't have done anything like that. In May, a preview version of its image-to-video feature took first place in the Arena, but by November, citing.

# :20 Bot增长和算力租赁

another leaderboard, its image-to-video ranked 17th and text-to-video ranked 16th. Looking at the leaderboards separately, there are many new competitors currently in the lead. The boss might be losing patience, but he hasn't resorted to cheating in this regard. What about the lawsuits? There have actually been some. Grok was initially the wildest among public-facing online image generators— everyone, please note this adjective, I'm talking about public-facing online tools.

# :19 xAI重心转向编程与Bot

If you compare it to image models you can download and fine-tune yourself, those are certainly much wilder. But for a platform this big to actually take responsibility and dare to let you generate those images—some of which I think couldn't even be covered by the term "borderline"—Grok is the only one that dared to release such capabilities directly. On March 26, an Amsterdam court issued an immediately enforceable injunction requiring xAI to stop generating and distributing non-consensual deepfake images involving.

# :22 Grok下一代模型路线

Dutch residents. Failure to comply could result in a daily fine of 100,000 euros , up to a maximum of 10 million euros. That is a violation of the upper limit of the injunction. There are also people suing for damages in the US. In a California case, xAI wanted to pause it and move it to Texas, but the judge did not agree. Tencent likes to move cases to Shenzhen, specifically the Nanshan District Court, which is why Tencent is called the "Nanshan Must-Win Plaintiff. " xAI wanted to do the same thing; they.

# :40 AI漫剧需要的模型与生态

asked if they could answer the lawsuit in Texas instead of California. The judge in California did not agree. Right now, the compensation case hasn't reached a final verdict yet. The xAI listing document states very clearly that the xAI model will bring about lawsuits. It might annoy advertisers and could also affect product distribution. Musk originally pushed the boundaries to attract users to play, but as rules tightened, those who wanted that kind of effect naturally decreased compared to before.

# :18 Imagine的收入和广告难题

So, did this team build something that no one uses? Certainly not. xAI provided a set of data when it went public. By the end of March this year, that quarter, imaging generated an average of 10 billion images and over 2 billion videos per month. These were generation counts, so people were still playing with it quite intensely at the time. In March, when there was talk of closing S, Musk immediately said Imagine would double down. After the court injunction was issued,.

# :53 马斯克的裁员决策风格

xAI still released new video and image models. That month he was also arguing with Nolan, because he felt Nolan chose Black and transgender actors to film The Odyssey. Musk said I must use Grok to film one, believing the long-form version would finally be delivered. In October, they released a 7-minute first episode. With an external production team involved all day, just weeks after it came out, he fired the entire team.

# :00 算力押注与用户期待

You can't explain the intervening months with just one lawsuit; saying no one was playing it doesn't match the data. What actually forced Musk's hand were other factors; in early November, a group of paid users on X started bashing Grok. Some said they did nothing all night, and their weekly limit was cut in half or simply wiped out. Some said it used to take days to hit the limit. Now it happens in just a few tasks; others complain that work it used to handle is now being fabricated or forgotten. Even local commands that used to run fine are now being rejected. A user named Greg said he used Grok for work and his quota suddenly ran out. It delayed his own business, and he wanted to cancel his Super Grok Heavy subscription. This "Heavy" was an old premium tier; at the time, users explicitly stated they paid $ 300 a month, while the $ 30 a. month plan was a later merged package combining Grok, Cursor Pro, and Premium benefits. The one Greg specifically named was " Heavy," the $ 300 tier. In the Cursor community, people are saying problems are piling up; users who already canceled feel there's a sudden downgrade, possibly due to model routing , context tools, or permission issues. Someone preparing to purchase Grok for. their company said they were initially quite satisfied with the trial. But just before signing, the quality fluctuated too much, and they couldn't even choose their models, so the deal was cut. If the company really put their work into it and something went wrong, the whole process would just halt. On November 1st, Musk himself replied on X, essentially saying that the cost of providing Grok services is unsustainably high relative to revenue. Later, he said they were fixing efficiency and task performance. On. November 10th, Beijing time, the official team reset the weekly quota for all Grok users again, and at that moment , you could get back to work. How much work can you get done for the same money next week? Let's think, why would anyone use Grok? You give it a task, and it has its own cloud computer; it can open a browser, use tools, write results into documents , and even if you close your laptop, it keeps running. A task can repeatedly call the model; if.

it goes wrong, it can go back and fix it , verify it after, and users feel the effort is sufficient because the server has provided good models and enough computing power. During the October earnings call, the SpaceX president said that by early October, Grok already had 800,000 paid subscribers. That's more than double the number from the previous month. This includes users who originally bought X Premium or Premium +. Now that customers are actively using it, the boss himself says the costs are hard to bear. And now. there's one more project eating up GPU capacity—this one. Projects for AI video and AI image generation are certainly too expensive to keep running. Some might ask, is Musk really short on GPUs ? Isn't he one of the few people in the U.S. most capable of building data centers? He has certainly built many, but if you look at these projects. Some are still in fundraising; the $ 40 billion is money raised but not yet spent, some are under construction, and some have machines that are powered on and networked. They are at different stages, and the. only ones currently running are the Memphis cluster and the others. In May, they announced they had secured full capacity for the first cluster, claiming to have used over 220,000 GPUs that month, with contracts expanding further. The November prospectus stated that by December, all computing power is expected to be fully onboard, totaling about $ 3.1 billion per month, with earlier batches already online. Although people online are saying he might cancel subscriptions early next year, as of now, I haven't seen any official notice. SpaceX has also signed computing power contracts with Google. Under full capacity terms, it’s $ 920 million per month; the financial reports don't clarify exactly which batch of cards goes to whom. This is the interesting part; the SpaceX CFO said in the October earnings call that they are comparing renting out. compute to cloud customers versus running their own products to see which has better margins. If you are the head of Grok and say, " Give me another batch of cards, I need to push my video model further," You have to compare the same batch of cards against two types of business: do I rent them to Google or Anthropic, or keep them for my own people to run Grok? After comparing, they realize it doesn't work; the return on investment for this thing just isn't high enough. That’s why.

I say when everyone else was complaining about Grok and canceling subscriptions, Musk decisively cut the entire imaging team. Why would he rather keep pouring money into the bot? After seeing those 800,000 users, Musk had already started betting heavily on programming. He acquired Cursor in the spring, finalized the merger in August, and reached a valuation of $ 60 billion. What Cursor brought in were developer customers, a product team, and people. who train models. Both sides released 4.5 in July and 4.6 in August; the bot's volume grew, proving this tech could be used for other office tasks. Look at how the staff changed. At xAI’s founding, there were 11 co-founders besides Musk; by the end of March this year, all 11 had resigned. Not a single one remained. One thing is directly relevant today: Igor Babuschkin was in charge of images and part of the programming functions; the Financial Times reported that Musk was dissatisfied with the programming. progress. He stripped him of his main responsibilities. Right around that time , two product and engineering leads from Cursor joined xAI. You were originally the person working on video. From that moment on, we knew the boss was holding people accountable for programming progress. Later, McNair, who previously managed Starlink, took over xAI. Bloomberg saw his memo to employees, and the goal was to catch up to Claude. After the Cursor acquisition, The Information reported that the Cursor CEO. reports to Musk, while the other two co-founders took charge of pre-training and machine learning management. The original Cursor team is still working on products, and Grok was developed with the direct involvement of Cursor employees before the acquisition . You ask if there's office politics involved? Who gets to report directly to the boss ? Who can show paying users? Who is responsible for the next-generation model? Everything has changed. As for whether a certain faction suggested getting rid of imaging, we don’t have evidence for that, and we shouldn't speculate from the outside. I think more importantly, Musk now really sees a path to catching up to the best models; 4.7 has already made long-running code execution and knowledge work a priority. In November, he said 4.8's pre-training was finished and it was undergoing reinforcement learning, ready to be rolled out to some bot users first.

For this generation, they rewrote the reinforcement learning and inference software in C and C ++. Musk himself admitted that 4.8 still doesn't beat Opus 3.5. Some people asked earlier if Grok was just taking other people's work and modifying it. This time, they are finally building it from scratch themselves. Grok's early image generation was indeed modified from Black Forest Labs 'Flux, and later they released Aura, where they disclosed the architecture. Musk also admitted in court that a portion of the training used output from OpenAI models. As for exactly how much external output was used for Grok 2 and Imaging, nobody has calculated that figure. Grok 1 released its self-trained base weights a long time ago. This time with Grok 2, it is very clear that Musk wants to keep the key engineering of how models are trained and run in his own hands; the more work the bot does, the more valuable the cost saved per task becomes. This reminds me of Liang Wenfeng, something I mentioned on my show before . When information from his communication with investors was accidentally leaked, he said he wouldn't build video models or world models because that isn't the path to AGI. It's a good business, but it's not on that path; I need to catch up on the model first—these are the trade-offs that those with limited compute must make. So, Musk made a trade-off at this time, which was to shut down both video and. image generation. Actually, OpenAI made a similar trade-off; they turned off Sora and now only keep the image model here. As for the other side, Anthropic's Claude has never been able to generate video or images; it can only understand them, but cannot generate them. In China , DeepSeek and Kimi are also only capable of understanding images and video, but cannot generate them. So, looking ahead, isn't Musk going to film Odyssey? Why not use Grok to make AI dramas? AI is so hot right now. He has X as an entry point; why not let creators use Imaging directly to make these AI dramas? I think there are two issues here. The first is that AI drama creation has already been pushed to a very, very industrialized level by these people in China. You have to compare model capabilities directly; if your model isn't good enough, no one will use it. Current top AI models include: first,.

Kling 1.5; second, Kling 4.0; and Alibaba's Wanx, known as Tongyi Wanxiang 3.0. These three are the most widely used ones right now. You might ask, if I still want to watch "trashy" short dramas—you know, the informal kind—what are those made with? They are made with MiniMax-video-01 because it's open-source. Once you take it and do some fine-tuning, you can definitely make these kinds of short dramas. We mentioned that Grok Imaging's image-to-video and text-to-video. rankings are stuck in 15th or 16th place , so nobody is going to use it. What is the other reason? If you want to build up AI, you need massive human operations, which is something Musk finds hard to accept. Look at models that have Jimeng, Tomato Novel, Hongguo distribution, tech support from partner teams, and traffic support programs—you need a whole pile of these things to pull up the entire ecosystem. Google has YouTube behind it, and Google’s own video models are actually doing quite well. YouTube is now also starting to lean into short-form dramas . Now, on the site, you can organize and play content by season and episode. In the past, when you watched a short video on YouTube and swiped, it would randomly push a new one. Now, after watching one short drama episode and swiping up, you can watch the whole season in order. Meta is also doing this now; they have. Make-A-Scene and Movie Gen which are quite good, and Meta is likely planning to keep pushing them on Instagram Reels . But X won't waste the effort. On one hand, they don't have the manpower to operate this, and on the other, they lack the computing power to chase the top spots in video models. If you want to catch up to the leaders, you need to burn compute to iterate the model, and they can't manage that right now. After Grok Imaging generated so many. videos and images, did it actually bring real revenue to the X platform? Although it increased traffic, as we mentioned earlier, it generates edge-case content. The edge-case images hurt the interests of advertisers, so advertisers don't want to run ads on the platform anymore. He is currently busy trying to collect 8 dollars or 30 dollars from people every day. So, generating a ton of these videos is just pure consumption of computing power —purely spending money without earning back what you should.

Therefore, it had to be cut. Besides, Musk has no plans to do short dramas. If it were a different company with a different boss, would this team be cut so quickly? Probably not, and that is what makes Musk different from other bosses. Do you remember when he bought Twitter and carried a kitchen sink into the office? At the time, Twitter had 7,800 employees. That was quickly slashed down to about 1,500 people. He is someone who absolutely does not tolerate any dead. weight. He realized that his direction is now Grok, and his focus is on personal agents. So I need the authority to get this done . The surplus compute I have, I'll rent it out to OpenAI or Google. With the remaining compute falling short , I must preserve my final hope. Since this current team isn't making money and chasing GPT would require burning even more compute, I wouldn't wait a single minute—I'd just cut them off immediately. This decision must have been very abrupt. , which is exactly the kind of thing Musk likes to do. Musk is now consolidating his people and capital, betting it all on one hand. For him, the general model needs to keep chasing GPT, and he must find a way to monetize it. For the users, if you want me to entrust my work to you, you need to guarantee the quota and service clearly. Which teams you keep is none of my business; whether you can finish the work I give you tomorrow according to my. expectations is what matters most. In my judgment, he is allocating the limited compute to Grok-bot and the next generation of Grok large models. Alright , that’s all for today’s story. Thank you for listening. Please like, hit the notification bell, join our Discord discussion group, and interested and capable friends are also welcome to join our paid channel. Goodbye. Yeah.
